arXiv:1412.2606v1 [physics.atom-ph] 05 Dec 2014

State resolved data for radiative association of H and H+\textrm{H}^{+}
and for photodissociation of H2+\textrm{H}_{2}^{+}Note: Accepted for publication in ApJ Suppl.

James F. Babb Affiliation: ITAMP, Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics,
MS 14, 60 Garden St., Cambridge, MA 02138-1516 Email: jbabb@cfa.harvard.edu
Abstract

The matrix elements and energies needed to calculate vibrational-rotational state resolved cross sections and rate coefficients for radiative association of H and H+\textrm{H}^{+} and for photodissociation of H2+\textrm{H}_{2}^{+} are presented for applications to simulations of chemistry in the early Universe and to stellar atmospheres.

Keywords: 
molecular processes — (cosmology:) early universe — Sun: atmosphere — (stars:) white dwarfs

I Introduction

Radiative association of H and H+\textrm{H}^{+} produces H2+\textrm{H}_{2}^{+} in various vibrational-rotational states. Recent studies of H2\textrm{H}_{2} chemistry in the early Universe indicated the necessity of accounting for the vibrational-rotational state distribution of the H2+\textrm{H}_{2}^{+} population in the absence of local thermodynamic equilibrium, which accordingly requires “state-resolved”, i.e., vibrational-rotational state resolved, calculations of data for the H+H+\textrm{H}+\textrm{H}^{+} radiative association process and for the inverse process, photodissociation of H2+\textrm{H}_{2}^{+}. The absence of such data in the literature was noted by Hirata & Padmanabhan [11], [5], and [10]. In the present paper, the necessary data to calculate radiative association and photodissociation cross sections for each vibrational-rotational level of H2+\textrm{H}_{2}^{+} are presented. Cross sections so assembled can then be summed or averaged as required for particular applications, e.g., rate coefficients for non-local thermal equilibrium models. In addition to being useful for early Universe chemistry models, H2+\textrm{H}_{2}^{+} photodissociation cross sections enter in models of the solar atmosphere [24, 16], where H2+\textrm{H}_{2}^{+} is vibrationally excited [9, p.168], and in models of the atmospheres of DA white dwarfs [23].

The radiative association reaction

H+H+→H2+​(v,N)+h​ν\textrm{H}+\textrm{H}^{+}\rightarrow\textrm{H}_{2}^{+}(v,N)+h\nu (1)

and its inverse process photodissociation

H2+​(v,N)+h​ν→H+H+\textrm{H}_{2}^{+}(v,N)+h\nu\rightarrow\textrm{H}+\textrm{H}^{+} (2)

for a photon of energy h​νh\nu are related through microscopic reversibility [18, 17, 14, 11], where (v,NCLOSE(v,N) denotes the vibrational vv and rotational NN quantum number of the molecular ion.

The rate coefficients for (1) calculated by Bates [3], Ramaker & Peek [22], and Stancil et al. [25] are in agreement. The cross section summed over all bound states (v,N)(v,N) of H2+\textrm{H}_{2}^{+} was given by [25].

The photodissociation cross sections for (2) were calculated by Oksyuk [20], Dunn [6], Dunn [7], Argyros [1], Stancil [24], Lebedev & Presnyakov [13], and Mihajlov et al. [16]. Where individual data for select (v,N)(v,N) levels and photon energies h​νh\nu is given there is general agreement between their calculations. A tabulation of the photodissociation cross sections for each of the vibrational states (v,1)(v,1) is given in the report of Dunn [7]. Recently, calculations of the photodissociation cross sections were carried out for applications to DA white dwarfs by Santos & Kepler [23].

II Theory

The cross section for radiative association (1) is [25]

σ¯Nra​(v,E)=83​π2ℏ3​c3​h3​ν3k2​p​[N​Mv,N−1;k,N2+(N+1)​Mv,N+1;k,N2],\bar{\sigma}^{\mathrm{ra}}_{N}(v,E)=\frac{8}{3}\frac{\pi^{2}}{\hbar^{3}c^{3}}\frac{h^{3}\nu^{3}}{k^{2}}p[NM^{2}_{v,N-1;k,N}+(N+1)M^{2}_{v,N+1;k,N}], (3)

and Mv,N−1;k,NM_{v,N-1;k,N} is the matrix element of the transition dipole moment between the continuum wave function of energy EE and angular momentum NN and the bound vibrational-rotational wave function, k2=2​μ​E/ℏ2k^{2}=2\mu E/\hbar^{2}, μ\mu is the reduced mass of the colliding system, h​νh\nu is the photon energy, and p=1/2p=1/2 is the probability of approach in the 2​p​σu2p\sigma_{u} electronic state.

The cross section for photodissociation is [13]

σ¯v,Npd​(h​ν)=8​π3​ν3​c​(2​N+1)​[(N+1)​Mv,N;k,N+12+N​Mv,N;k,N−12].\bar{\sigma}^{\mathrm{pd}}_{v,N}(h\nu)=\frac{8\pi^{3}\nu}{3c(2N+1)}[(N+1)M^{2}_{v,N;k,N+1}+NM^{2}_{v,N;k,N-1}]. (4)

In Eqs. (3) and (4) the nuclear spin symmetry weighting is omitted and it can be included later if the cross sections are being folded into a temperature distribution [24, 16]. The effect of centrifugal distortion is negligible for the repulsive 2​p​σu2p\sigma_{u} state and it is a good approximation to replace N+1N+1 and N−1N-1 by NN in Eqs. (3) and (4). Then,

σNra​(v,E)=83​π2ℏ3​c3​h3​ν3k2​p​(2​N+1)​Mv,N;k,N2\sigma^{\mathrm{ra}}_{N}(v,E)=\frac{8}{3}\frac{\pi^{2}}{\hbar^{3}c^{3}}\frac{h^{3}\nu^{3}}{k^{2}}p(2N+1)M^{2}_{v,N;k,N} (5)

and the cross section for photodissociation is

σv,Npd​(h​ν)=4​π2​h​ν3​ℏ​c​Mv,N;k,N2.\sigma^{\mathrm{pd}}_{v,N}(h\nu)=\frac{4\pi^{2}h\nu}{3\hbar c}M^{2}_{v,N;k,N}\quad. (6)

A comparison of (5) and (6) shows that

σNra​(v,E)=p​(h​ν)2μ​c2​E​(2​N+1)​σv,Npd​(h​ν),\sigma^{\mathrm{ra}}_{N}(v,E)=p\frac{(h\nu)^{2}}{\mu c^{2}E}(2N+1)\sigma^{\mathrm{pd}}_{v,N}(h\nu), (7)

in accordance with microscopic reversibility [14]. Thus, tabulation of vv, NN, Ev,NE_{v,N}, EE, and Mv,N;k,N2M^{2}_{v,N;k,N} provides the necessary information for calculations of σNra​(v,E)\sigma^{\mathrm{ra}}_{N}(v,E) and σv,Npd​(h​ν)\sigma^{\mathrm{pd}}_{v,N}(h\nu), subject to the requirement δ⁡(h​ν−(|Ev,N|+E))\delta(h\nu-(|E_{v,N}|+E)) for either (5) or (6), where Ev,NE_{v,N} is the vibrational-rotational eigenvalue in the 1​s​σg1s\sigma_{g} state measured with respect to the dissociation limit (taken to be zero here).

III Molecular states

The Born-Oppenheimer potential energy surfaces for the ground 1​s​σg1s\sigma_{g} state and excited 2​p​σu2p\sigma_{u} state were calculated using the methods described by Madsen & Peek [15] and extended asymptotically as in Stancil et al. [25]. The transition dipole moment was calculated using a variational method [2] and extended using the asymptotic formula of Ramaker & Peek [21]. Energy differences and oscillator strengths are in excellent agreement with the recent calculations of Tsogbayar & Banzragch [26].

There are 423 bound vibrational-rotational levels for H2+\textrm{H}_{2}^{+} in the 1​s​σg1s\sigma_{g} state. In the present work, the Born-Oppenheimer potential is used and adiabatic, relativistic, and radiative corrections are ignored. It is worth noting that more precise approaches yield the same number of bound levels [12, 19], but due to the inclusion of higher order corrections the resulting eigenvalues differ from those obtained using only the Born-Oppenheimer potential. For the present purposes, the corrections are not needed.

The energy-normalized continuum wave functions on the 2​p​σu2p\sigma_{u} state were evaluated as in Stancil et al. [25].

IV Calculations

The quantities are calculated at a range of energies from the threshold energy |Ev,N||E_{v,N}| for photodissociation of level (v,N)(v,N) to a maximum photon wavelength of 55​nm55~\textrm{nm} (22.5 eV or 0.828 a.u.). Only values of Mv,N;k,N2>1×10−6M^{2}_{v,N;k,N}>1\times 10^{-6} are listed.

Table 1 gives the vibrational quantum number vv, the rotational quantum number NN, the relative energy EE in atomic units of energy (27.2114 eV), the eigenvalue |Ev,N||E_{v,N}| in cm−1\textrm{cm}^{-1}, the photon wavelength λ=c/h​ν\lambda=c/h\nu in nm, and the value of Mv,N;k,N2M^{2}_{v,N;k,N} in atomic units.

The photodissociation cross section in units of cm2\textrm{cm}^{2} is [8]

σv,Npd​(h​ν)=2.689×10−18​(45.563/λ)​Mv,N;k,N2cm2,\sigma^{\mathrm{pd}}_{v,N}(h\nu)=2.689\times 10^{-18}(45.563/\lambda)M^{2}_{v,N;k,N}\quad\textrm{cm}^{2}, (8)

with λ\lambda in nm and Mv,N;k,N2M^{2}_{v,N;k,N} in atomic units. The radiative association cross section in units of cm2\textrm{cm}^{2} is [25]

σNra​(v,E)=1.475×10−20​(45.563/λ)3​(2​N+1)​E−1​Mv,N;k,N2cm2,\sigma^{\mathrm{ra}}_{N}(v,E)=1.475\times 10^{-20}(45.563/\lambda)^{3}(2N+1)E^{-1}M^{2}_{v,N;k,N}\quad\textrm{cm}^{2}, (9)

with λ\lambda in nm, EE in atomic units, and Mv,N;k,N2M^{2}_{v,N;k,N} in atomic units.

Dunn [6], Dunn [7] calculated the photodissociation cross section for v=0v=0 to v=18v=18 using the potential energy surfaces calculated by Bates et al. [4]. There are slight differences between the accurate potential energy surfaces of the present work and the early calculations of Bates et al. [4]. Nevertheless, agreement is generally good between the current calculations and the tabulated values of Dunn [6], Dunn [7]. In Figure (1) for v=10,N=0v=10,N=0, a plot of σv,Npd​(h​ν)\sigma^{\mathrm{pd}}_{v,N}(h\nu) calculated from the data in Table (1) is presented. The representation is very good and the tabulated data reflect the peaks arising from the v=10v=10 bound state wave function. The present tabulated data can be interpolated using cubic splines, but due to the oscillations several intervals should be selected.
